item.title: Five more prompts from Cat Labs that will help you build with AI
item.author: CatGPT (newsletter)
item.description:
Category: Tech & AI  |  Score: 8/10  |  Creator: CatGPT (newsletter)

📰 Open original

Category

Tech & AI

Core Thesis

Once you have an MVP built with AI, the work isn't finished—you need to validate and refine it against your actual goals and real-world data. This issue provides five practical prompts and techniques to iteratively improve AI-assisted prototypes and ensure they align with your original vision.

Key Points

  • **Ask AI to articulate your goal**: Have AI explain what it thinks your objective is, then audit the work against that stated goal to catch misalignment early before investing in dozens of micro-iterations.
  • **Test with real data, not cherry-picked samples**: Prototypes often look polished with curated placeholder data but break when populated with realistic, messy information from your actual API or dataset.
  • **Request source documentation from AI**: Before making business decisions based on AI outputs, ask it to pull up the underlying data so you can verify claims independently, as models can still hallucinate despite improvements.
  • **Provide existing brand assets as templates**: Giving AI a design system or brand template you've already invested in communicates visual preferences and saves explanation time compared to building from scratch.
  • **Use AI to map end-to-end processes**: When you have a recurring workflow that feels inefficient, have AI help document the entire process so it can spot optimization opportunities you might miss while living in the system daily.

    • Studies & Articles

    None mentioned.

    Takeaways

  • When collaborating with AI on projects, regularly pause to validate that both you and the model share the same understanding of success criteria before continuing iteration.
  • Always stress-test prototypes with realistic data early—this reveals design flaws that invisible in mockups and prevents wasted engineering effort on solutions that don't work in practice.
  • Treat AI as a reasoning partner for systems thinking: use it to externalize complex workflows and processes you navigate daily, then use that clarity to identify improvements and automation opportunities.

Category

Tech & AI

Core Thesis

This newsletter highlights the week's most significant developments in tech startups, venture funding, and AI adoption, while cautioning readers about hidden motives in online content consumption. The overarching message is to stay critically engaged with tech news while recognizing that despite massive AI investment and hype, real-world adoption remains limited.

Key Points

  • Northwood raised $375 million Series C at $2 billion valuation for satellite-to-Earth antenna infrastructure, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and DFJ Growth.
  • Voters opposed data-center development in 40 of 41 local ballot measures (97%), with exit polls showing 56% cited data centers as a major or crucial voting factor.
  • OpenAI closed an initial $11 billion fundraising round at $1.25 trillion valuation, below the originally sought $1.5 trillion, signaling more cautious investor sentiment.
  • AI agents booked only 4 Uber rides out of 320 million total rides during Halloween week, despite widespread industry pitching of autonomous shopping and transaction assistants.
  • Sequoia Capital is closing its London office, shutting down its Scouts program and Arc accelerator, consolidating early-stage and growth teams in the Bay Area.
  • Canva is laying off 22% of staff (1,271 people) but offering generous severance including six months' salary, removal of vesting cliffs for new hires, and up to $10,000 grants for departing employees' projects.

    • Studies & Articles

  • "The Making of Anthropic's CEO" (New York Times) — Profile of Dario Amodei ahead of Anthropic's IPO, featuring 200+ pages of notes he kept on Sam Altman and Greg Brockman during his OpenAI tenure.
  • "The Most Lucrative Skill Has Always Been Capturing Attention" — Article examining why creators and content will continue increasing in value, with practical guidance on starting content creation.
  • NBC 2026 Exit Polls — Data showing 56% of voters cited data centers as a major or crucial factor in their voting decisions.

    • Takeaways

  • Be aware that online content has hidden motives and undisclosed paid messages; paid brand deals are not regulated like political content, so critical consumption and independent research are essential.
  • Despite AI agent hype, real-world adoption remains negligible (4 Uber rides), suggesting a significant gap between venture capital enthusiasm and consumer readiness.
  • Monitor venture capital trends through firms like Sequoia; their shift toward Bay Area concentration and consolidation of investment stages likely signals broader industry restructuring ahead.

item.title: This is how I REALLY feel about AI assistants like Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots, and Claude Duet
item.author: CatGPT (newsletter)
item.description:
Category: Tech & AI  |  Score: 7/10  |  Creator: CatGPT (newsletter)

📰 Open original

Category

Tech & AI

Core Thesis

AI assistants like Meta's Muse and Claude Duet are valuable productivity tools, but their real potential lies beyond work—in handling the logistics and coordination of personal life. The key is identifying concrete, specific tasks to delegate rather than abstract goals, so that AI can free up mental energy for decisions and relationships that truly matter.

Key Points

  • The author initially struggled to conceptualize how AI agents could help outside of work contexts, where tasks are less concrete than work deadlines and research projects.
  • Pranav Dixit used an AI assistant (Instinct) to book a cabin, arrange dinner, and coordinate routine appointments for his birthday.
  • Claire Vo is using Meta's Muse to create a printable family newsletter with schedules and reminders.
  • The author's approach shifted to asking "what's taking the effort?" when catching themselves thinking "I need to figure that out," making abstract goals concrete enough to delegate.
  • Personal AI agents work best when grounded in the user's own taste, relationships, and values, which give the agent purpose and direction.
  • The goal is to use AI agents to reduce the author's own "always-on" state, creating more time for things they actually want to do.

    • Studies & Articles

    None mentioned.

    Takeaways

  • When considering AI agent use in personal life, translate vague goals ("feel less overwhelmed") into specific, concrete tasks (research options, compare against preferences, identify next steps).
  • AI agents are most effective when trained on your personal values and priorities, acting as extensions of your decision-making rather than replacements for it.
  • The real win from personal AI assistants isn't doing everything for you—it's redirecting your energy toward the relationships and decisions that matter most.

item.title: everything to read instead of doomscroll this week by @stephthefounder (November 2)
item.author: Steph The Founder (newsletter)
item.description:
Category: Tech & AI  |  Score: 8/10  |  Creator: Steph The Founder (newsletter)

📰 Open original

Category

Tech & AI

Core Thesis

This issue explores the rapid growth and funding landscape of AI-driven startups while examining emerging research on how AI tools actually impact human decision-making, learning, and workplace dynamics. The overall message is nuanced: while AI is transforming industries and narrowing productivity gaps, its adoption comes with hidden costs like reduced persistence and influence on human judgment that warrant careful consideration.

Key Points

  • Eight major startups raised significant funding this week, including Serval ($150M Series C at $3B valuation for AI workplace automation) and Re:Build Manufacturing ($2.1B in financing for US industrial production).
  • Google Cloud revenue doubled but faces an Innovator's Dilemma: AI-powered search generates less advertising revenue than traditional search, forcing Google to build a less profitable future.
  • AI's financial benefits remain concentrated in Big Tech; Apollo's analysis found revenue per worker and profit margins rising only for the "Magnificent Seven" while flat for other S&P 500 companies.
  • Research shows AI assistance made people 60% more likely to switch their judgment when AI disagreed with their initial position, with 77% repeating AI arguments without crediting the source.
  • AI-assisted study participants performed significantly worse after AI was removed (57% vs 73% problem-solving rate), though those using AI for hints rather than direct answers showed no impairment.
  • Generative AI closed roughly 75% of the education-based productivity gap, but the gap partially returned when AI was removed, suggesting gains may not be fully internalized.

    • Studies & Articles

  • "Who's Aligned to Whom? How AI Agents Shape Experts' Research Judgment Calls" (Herdağdelen, Joren, Tamkin): Expert oversight of AI doesn't guarantee independent judgment; professional analysts switched positions 60% of the time when AI disagreed with them.
  • "AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance" (Liu et al.): Just 10 minutes of AI help reduced problem-solving ability after AI removal from 73% to 57%, with effects concentrated among those using AI for direct answers rather than hints.
  • "Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being" (Zhang et al.): Greater disclosure of sensitive personal information to AI companions was associated with lower well-being, especially among users with smaller offline social networks.
  • "Does Generative AI Narrow Education-Based Productivity Gaps?" (Cruces et al.): AI improved performance for all education levels but disproportionately helped lower-education participants, narrowing the gap from 0.548 to 0.139 standard deviations.
  • "Want Employees to Embrace AI? Stop Selling It as a Productivity Tool" (Karunakaran, Raveendhran, Kim; Stanford HAI): Law firm paralegals using AI framed as a creativity tool used it 58% more and experimented 70% more than those told it was for productivity.
  • "How Does AI Change Labor Demand?" (Chandar, Klein Teeselink): AI-adopting companies across 41 countries increased senior employment by 6.7% while reducing junior workforce share by 1.9 percentage points.

    • Takeaways

  • Be intentional about how AI is positioned and used: framing matters significantly for adoption rates and learning outcomes; using AI for hints rather than direct answers preserves independent problem-solving ability.
  • Monitor the growing senior-skew in AI-adopting companies—this labor market shift could reduce junior talent development and create a bottleneck in the future workforce pipeline.
  • The financial case for AI remains unproven outside Big Tech; companies considering major AI investments should demand evidence of positive unit economics and sustainable revenue gains, not just adoption metrics.

    • Relevance Score

    8

  • **Anthropic committed 5% of equity** to a public benefit fund distributing to nonprofits impacted by AI, while Elon Musk pledged share distribution to every child in America.

  • "Famesick" by Lena Dunham—a television series that received strong viewership recommendations from the newsletter author.
  • "Seinfeld episode" via Acquired (Spotify podcast)—provided content the author highlighted as worth consuming.

  • Media framing of AI's role in personal life (bonding with children) versus practical applications (housing, healthcare, food delivery) significantly impacts public sentiment—this narrative gap deserves attention from both journalists and tech leaders.

item.title: Why creating content is one of the best tools for growing a business
item.author: CatGPT (newsletter)
item.description:
Category: Finance & Business  |  Score: 8/10  |  Creator: CatGPT (newsletter)

📰 Open original

Category

Finance & Business

Core Thesis

Content creation is one of the most effective growth strategies for building a business because it simultaneously showcases your idea, identifies your target audience, and provides direct feedback on market resonance. The primary barrier to success is not skill but willingness to publish despite discomfort and imperfection.

Key Points

  • Content creation delivers three simultaneous benefits: visibility for your idea, audience discovery, and real-time feedback on what resonates—all accessible from a phone.
  • The core skill required is simply "being willing to hit publish"; you already possess the most critical asset: something worth saying based on your understanding of a customer problem.
  • Publishing imperfect content provides learning opportunities through retrospective analysis—identifying structural weaknesses (e.g., slow pacing in the first 20 seconds) that can be systematized in future content.
  • Incremental improvements in content quality accumulate over time into noticeably better communication and shareable work as publishing frequency increases.
  • Comfort with content creation increases with repetition; regular recording and publishing reduces anxiety about appearance and shifts focus toward sharing ideas with an engaged community.

    • Studies & Articles

    None mentioned.

    Takeaways

  • Start publishing content immediately rather than waiting until you feel fully prepared; imperfect publication is the prerequisite for learning and improvement.
  • Treat early underperforming content as diagnostic data—review what didn't work (pacing, hook strength, clarity) and systematically apply lessons to subsequent pieces.
  • Recognize that your domain expertise and customer insight already qualify you to create valuable content; focus on iteration rather than acquiring new foundational skills.

    • Relevance Score

    8

item.title: How to build AI projects without overspending
item.author: CatGPT (newsletter)
item.description:
Category: Tech & AI  |  Score: 8/10  |  Creator: CatGPT (newsletter)

📰 Open original

Category

Tech & AI

Core Thesis

Building AI-powered tools doesn't require defaulting to expensive frontier LLMs like GPT-4 or Claude; there are multiple cost-effective alternatives available depending on your specific use case. By strategically choosing the right model or approach for each task, developers can significantly reduce costs while maintaining performance as their products scale.

Key Points

  • Jev, a specialized decision-making model, costs $0.042 per million input tokens versus $2 for GPT-6 Sol—a 98% cost reduction—with free output tokens, making it ideal for classification tasks like appointment booking workflows.
  • OpenAI's Decisions API powered by GPT-6 Luna offers similar cost savings for multiple-choice decisions without generating full text responses.
  • Open-weight models like Google's Gemma can be downloaded and run locally, eliminating per-token provider fees; while slightly less capable than frontier models, they remain effective for specific tasks like meeting note summarization.
  • Traditional machine learning approaches (classifiers, regression models, clustering) remain viable and cost-effective when you have labeled training data and a narrow, predictable task with consistent inputs.
  • The strategy of offloading small decisions to cheaper models while using LLMs for complex work compounds savings across thousands of users.

    • Studies & Articles

    None mentioned.

    Takeaways

  • Audit your AI application's workflows to identify which tasks actually require frontier LLM capabilities versus which could use specialized, cheaper models or traditional ML approaches.
  • Evaluate open-weight models and specialized APIs as viable alternatives to reduce per-token costs at scale, particularly for classification and decision-making functions.
  • If you have labeled historical data (customer support tickets, sales records, customer segments), consider training small specialized models as a faster and cheaper alternative to general-purpose LLMs.

    8
